# Art bible

The look of Open Kingdoms: a warm, readable, storybook-medieval city seen from
a high isometric-style camera. Chunky silhouettes, saturated identity colours,
hand-painted-looking textures, soft sun. Everything is **original** and
**generated by scripts** in `tools/blender/` — no downloaded or copied art.

If you add or change art, follow this document and update it in the same PR.

## Pipeline

```
tools/blender/atlas_layout.py   where every material and decal lives in the atlas (shared by both scripts below)
tools/blender/gen_textures.py   system Python (numpy + Pillow): paints atlas.png, ground_*.png, noise.png
tools/blender/okkit.py          modelling kit for Blender: boxes, roofs, towers, props, UVs, baked AO
tools/blender/build_buildings.py   12 buildings x 5 tiers  -> client/assets/models/<kind>_t<tier>.glb
tools/blender/build_scenery.py     wall, terrain, forests, props -> client/assets/models/scenery/*.glb
scripts/build_art.sh            runs all of the above and re-imports the Godot project
```

Everything is deterministic (fixed seeds), so regenerating without changing a
script produces the same assets. Commit the `.glb`, `.png` and their `.import`.

Visual check after any change (then **look** at the PNG):

```bash
$GODOT --path client -s res://tests/screenshot.gd -- <abs_out.png> [fixture.json] [camera_distance] [focus_x focus_z]
```

Fixtures: `client/tests/fixtures/showcase_city.json` (early city, tiers 1–3)
and `grand_city.json` (late city, tiers 4–5).

## Scale and orientation

- 1 Blender unit = 1 Godot unit = 1 city tile. Blender +Z is up.
- A building's footprint is `footprint x footprint` tiles from
  `data/buildings.yaml`. The model is centred on the origin, sits on z = 0 and
  must stay inside the footprint minus a 0.07 margin on every side (eaves and
  flags may overhang a little, ground-level geometry may not).
- Fronts (doors, signs, yards) face Blender **−Y** = Godot **+Z**: towards the
  camera. The camera (yaw 45°, pitch 50°, FOV 35°) sees the front and the +X
  side, so put detail there; back and left faces only need to be closed.
- Storybook proportions: walls are low (0.5–1.1), roofs are big (about 0.55 x
  span), doors and windows oversized, props (barrels, crates, carts) roughly
  1.5x "real" scale so they read from the default zoom.

## Silhouette rules

1. **Roof colour is identity.** One glance at the roof tells you the building,
   at every tier. Never reuse a roof colour for another kind.
2. **One prop story per building**, readable at default zoom: farm = field +
   hay (+ windmill later), lumber mill = log piles + saw wheel, quarry = rock
   face + cut blocks + crane, goldmine = mound + portal + cart + nuggets,
   storehouse = big doors + crates/barrels + hoist, barracks = training yard +
   dummies + shields, archery range = targets + lanes, stable = stalls +
   paddock + horses, siege workshop = forge chimney + catapult, hospital =
   healer's sign + herb garden, academy = columns + dome + tower.
3. **Height says importance.** City hall is the tallest thing in town; military
   buildings get towers; economy buildings stay low and wide.
4. Break the box: every building is at least two masses (hall + tower, shed +
   lean-to, mound + headframe) and has something in its yard.
5. No thin floating geometry below ~0.03 units; it shimmers at this camera.

## Tiers

`tier = 1 + (level - 1) div 5`, five tiers (levels 1–5, 6–10, 11–15, 16–20,
21–25). `BuildingFactory.tier_for_level` picks the model and falls back to a
lower tier if one is missing. Each tier must be visibly grander than the last
**and** keep the same roof colour and prop story.

| Tier | Theme | Walls | Roof | Ground pad | Extras |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | frontier wood | planks, corner posts | thatch | dirt | a prop or two |
| 2 | village | plaster + timber frame, stone skirt | tiles in identity colour | light cobble | chimney, more props |
| 3 | stone | brick, block foundation | tiles | cobble, stone kerb | first tower / second mass |
| 4 | ornate | warm brick | tiles + gold ridge | pale cobble | gold band, banners, standards, finials |
| 5 | majestic | marble | tiles/domes + gold | marble | spires, domes, columns, flags |

## Palette (sRGB)

Roof identity colours:

| Building | Hex | | Building | Hex |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| City hall | `#3f66bd` royal blue | | Barracks | `#b8402f` red |
| Farm | `#cf7a3c` orange | | Archery range | `#4f8a3f` green |
| Lumber mill | `#9a6b42` wood brown | | Stable | `#b0783a` ochre |
| Quarry | `#6f7682` slate | | Siege workshop | `#566070` iron blue |
| Goldmine | `#2f7a78` teal | | Hospital | `#58a98c` mint |
| Storehouse | `#c4633a` terracotta | | Academy | `#7a56b0` purple |

Materials and world (exact painted colours live in `gen_textures.py`):

| Use | Hex |
|---|---|
| Stone brick / block / rock | warm greys around `#a39c92` (never pure grey) |
| Plaster | warm off-white |
| Planks | `#a8713f` / `#8d5c33`, gaps `#3d2616` |
| Thatch | `#d8b45e`, shade `#8f6c2c` |
| Marble (tier 5) | tinted `#f6ecda` on walls, `#dccfba` on paving |
| Gold trim | painted gold texture, vertex colour white |
| Banners | red `#b8322b` with a sun (military/economy), blue `#2f55a4` with a star (city, academy) |
| Foliage | `#3f7a34` shade → `#9acb55` light, pines `#2f5f3a` → `#5f9a4a` |
| Grass | dry `#8fae4a` ↔ lush `#4f8f47` (large noise patches) |
| Road cobble / dirt | `#aaa091` / `#a07a52` |
| Water | deep `#216b99`, shallow `#54adc2` |
| Shadow tint | cool: AO and ambient lean blue (`#adc2f2`), sun is warm (`#fff0d1`) |

Saturation lives in roofs, banners and foliage; walls and ground stay muted so
the roofs pop. Avoid pure white, pure black and pure grey.

## Materials and textures

- **One atlas, one material.** `client/assets/textures/atlas.png` (2048²) holds
  17 tiling materials and 15 decals. Every generated model uses the single
  `client/assets/materials/atlas.tres` (applied by `BuildingFactory.apply_atlas`;
  the `.glb` files carry no materials), so a whole city is a handful of draw
  calls with no texture switches.
- **Tiling cells** hold two periods plus a wrapped gutter, and the kit splits
  any face longer than two periods, so tiles repeat seamlessly inside an atlas
  with mipmaps. Each material has a fixed world size per period
  (`atlas_layout.TILES`) so brick, shingle and plank scale is the same on every
  model.
- **Tint by vertex colour.** `roof_tiles`, `foliage`, `fabric`, `flat`, `rock`
  are painted neutral and multiplied by a vertex colour, so one texture serves
  every roof colour. Other materials are painted in their final colour and
  usually left untinted.
- **Baked light in vertex colours.** `Kit.bake_ao` ray-casts ambient occlusion
  per vertex (cool-tinted), and blobs/cones carry dark-to-light gradients. This
  gives grounding and depth even in the Compatibility renderer, where SSAO does
  not exist.
- **Decals** (windows, doors, shields, banners, wheels, targets) are quads
  mapped to their atlas cell, floated 1–3 cm off the wall.
- **Ground** is `client/assets/shaders/ground.gdshader`: world-space grass,
  dirt, cobble and rock textures (512², tiling, mipmapped) blended by a runtime
  road mask (`CityRoads.build_mask`, one pixel per tile, wobbled with noise for
  organic edges) and by terrain vertex-colour masks (R rock, G grass variation,
  B sand). Water is `water.gdshader`, opaque scrolling noise.
- Compatibility-safe by construction: no screen/depth textures, no
  transparency, no per-model materials, standard texture formats.

## Lighting (client/scenes/city.tscn)

- Sun: warm `#fff0d1`, energy 1.45, pitch −46°, yaw 28° → front and right faces
  lit, shadows fall up-left away from the camera. Soft PSSM shadows, 4096 map.
- Ambient: flat cool blue `#adc2f2` at 0.6 so shadows are blue-ish, not black.
- Filmic tonemap (white 1.6), slight contrast (1.06) and saturation (1.12).
- Light depth fog (`#bdd1eb`, density 0.0011) for aerial perspective on the
  hills; subtle glow for gold and marble; SSAO on Forward+ only (the baked AO
  carries the look where it is unavailable).
- The sky is never on screen at this camera, so the terrain extends ±112 units
  and rises into mountains at the edge.

## City dressing

- `CityDressing` (child of the city scene, outside `$Buildings`) owns terrain,
  water, wall, forests and props. It is decoration only: it never blocks or
  changes game state, and the full 40x40 grid stays buildable.
- Roads are computed by `CityRoads` (pure, unit-tested): two avenues from the
  four gates, a plaza two tiles around the city hall, and a shortest path from
  each building's door tile to the nearest road. Roads and props simply
  disappear under buildings.
- Props on free tiles are chosen by a per-tile hash (stable across clients and
  re-renders), denser near the wall. Lamp posts line the avenues.
- The wall stands just outside the grid (centre line 21.3 units from the
  middle), 1.4 high so it hides at most half a tile on the near sides.

## Budgets

| Asset | Triangles |
|---|---|
| Building, 2x2 footprint | 150–900 |
| Building, 3x3 footprint | 300–1 700 |
| City hall (4x4) | 1 000–2 500 |
| Small prop | 30–350 |
| City wall (whole ring) | ≤ 25 000 |
| Terrain | ≤ 25 000 |
| Forest scatter (one mesh) | ≤ 120 000 |

One mesh and one surface per `.glb`. Textures: one 2048² atlas, four 512²
ground textures, one 256² noise. No skeletal animation yet.

## Naming

- Buildings: `client/assets/models/<building id>_t<tier>.glb` (ids from
  `data/buildings.yaml`, tier 1–5). A Rust test
  (`kingdom-server/tests/repo_consistency.rs`) requires all five tiers and
  their `.import` for every building.
- Scenery: `client/assets/models/scenery/{terrain,city_wall,scatter}.glb` and
  `prop_<name>.glb`.
- Atlas cells: lowercase `snake_case` names in `atlas_layout.py`
  (`stone_brick`, `window_arch`, `banner_red`).
- Builders: `build_<kind>(k, t)` registered in `BUILDERS` with the footprint.

## Originality

Mechanics may resemble the genre; expression may not. Do not reference, trace
or imitate the art, UI, building designs or characters of Rise of Kingdoms or
any other game. Heraldry here is our own plain sun and star emblems.
